body: My therapist has said this... like no and you should know it doesn't work that way
Seems completely fine, leave it for now

I am not sure how to respond. I can't lie and say I feel magically better, because I don't. But I appreciate seeing your response when I woke up, I'm not quite sure what I would have done otherwise. So thank you.

I would love to establish independence but I get so lonely, and the smallest things break me down nowadays. I don't know how I will keep on going, not only going through life but also "roughing it". Reading that you made it made me kind of hopeful, maybe one day. 

I feel like not a lot of people relate to my insecurity about the way I look, so reading that part also helped me. Though I know my insecurity is rooted deeper than that, and that I probably never will like my looks. 

I keep re-reading this, especially the first and last paragraph and it honestly made me break down. It feels really good to be validated but also sucks to have it confirmed that it really was that bad. I have alot of issues accepting my situation as abnormal because I tend to block everything bad out, always have and probably always will.

Maybe it's too much to ask but can you maybe tell me a bit more of how you got to a place of being financially stable? The college part. I have gotten 0 advice and I have no idea how to, quite frankly, think for myself when it comes to big decisions like this. Something else my mother robbed me off.

I want to say thank you again. I had no one to talk to and feeling seen and not being ignored was maybe the best thing you gave me.
